output_test.dry_run_result: Phase 1 preflight PASS: prompt quality 9.6/10 DEPLOY, token budget OK, forecast all sections addressable, output-schema sub-engine found 0 sections/elements (expected — this is a multi-artifact research brief, not a single structured JSON response)
output_test.model_used: claude-opus-5 (passed through literally — NOT in output-test.py's MODEL_MAP, which only maps claude-opus-4-6/claude-sonnet-4-6/claude-haiku-4-5 to real API model IDs)
output_test.result: The call did not error (no API_ERROR string) but returned zero words of visible text while consuming the entire 1500-token budget. Two plausible, non-exclusive explanations, neither confirmable without deeper instrumentation than output-test.py provides: (1) the claude-opus-5 registry entry's own documented key_constraint — 'Safety classifiers can return stop_reason:refusal — handle before reading content' — and output-test.py's call_model() does not check response.stop_reason or handle non-text content blocks before concluding text='', or (2) adaptive thinking (on by default for this model) consumed the full 1500-token budget on internal reasoning for this large, dense, 10-question system prompt, leaving no budget for a visible answer. Layer-1 self-simulated assertions (tests.json) all failed against this empty output for the obvious reason that there was no text to check — this is not evidence of a defect in the prompt's content, since a proper invocation would need either thinking disabled (registry: 'capped at effort <= high') or a materially larger max_tokens.
output_test.recommendation_for_a_real_invocation: Use max_tokens well above 1500 (this is a 10-question research brief expected to produce multi-file, multi-thousand-word output over ~40 minutes of tool use, not a 1500-token answer) and check response.stop_reason before assuming empty content means failure.
